concepts.def: The smallest part of an element that can exist. All substances are made of atoms.
A substance made of only one kind of atom. There are about 100 different elements, shown in the periodic table.
The one- or two-letter code used to represent an atom of an element, eg O represents an atom of oxygen and Na represents an atom of sodium.
The table in which the elements are shown; it is supplied in the exam.
A substance containing two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions, represented by a formula built from the symbols of the atoms it was formed from.
A change that always forms one or more new substances and often involves a detectable energy change. Compounds can only be separated into elements by chemical reactions.
A representation of a reaction using the names of the reactants and products, with an arrow from reactants to products.
A representation of a reaction using symbols and formulae in which there are the same numbers of each type of atom on both sides.
(HT only) An equation showing the electrons lost or gained by one species, eg 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻.
(HT only) An equation showing only the ions and atoms that take part in the reaction, with spectator ions left out.
Two or more elements or compounds not chemically combined together; the chemical properties of each substance in the mixture are unchanged.
A physical process that separates an insoluble solid from a liquid; the solid stays on the filter paper as residue and the liquid passes through as filtrate.
A physical process in which the solvent is evaporated from a solution so that the dissolved solid is left behind as crystals.
A physical process that separates a solvent from a solution by boiling it off and condensing the vapour, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
A physical process that separates two or more miscible liquids using the differences between their boiling points.
A physical process that separates substances in a mixture by how they move with a solvent through paper.
A separation method that involves no chemical reaction, so no new substances are made.
An idea used to explain observations; new experimental evidence may lead to a model being changed or replaced.
The model that followed the discovery of the electron: the atom is a ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it.
The experiment whose results led to the conclusion that the mass of an atom is concentrated at the centre (nucleus) and that the nucleus is charged.
The model in which the mass of the atom is concentrated in a small charged nucleus; it replaced the plum pudding model.
Niels Bohr's adaptation of the nuclear model, in which electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances; his calculations agreed with experimental observations.
A positively charged particle in the nucleus; the positive charge of a nucleus is a whole number of these identical charges.
An uncharged particle in the nucleus; the experimental work of James Chadwick provided the evidence for neutrons, about 20 years after the nucleus became accepted.
A negatively charged particle, relative charge −1, that occupies energy levels (shells) around the nucleus.
Proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1.
The number of protons in an atom of an element. All atoms of a particular element have the same number of protons.
Atoms are very small, having a radius of about 0.1 nm (1 x 10⁻¹⁰ m).
The centre of the atom, containing almost all of its mass, with a radius less than 1/10 000 of that of the atom (about 1 x 10⁻¹⁴ m).
Proton 1, neutron 1, electron very small.
The sum of the protons and neutrons in an atom.
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
An atom that has lost or gained electrons, so the numbers of protons and electrons are no longer equal.
An average value for an element that takes account of the abundance of its isotopes.
A region around the nucleus that electrons occupy; electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels (innermost available shells) first.
The arrangement of electrons in the energy levels of an atom, written as numbers such as 2,8,1 for sodium or drawn as a diagram.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes what an atom is?
options: The smallest part of an element that can exist
The smallest particle that can ever exist
The smallest part of any compound that exists
A particle made of two or more atoms joined
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition of an atom.

mcqs.q: Which option gives the chemical symbols correctly?
options: So is sodium and Ox is oxygen
Na is sodium and O is oxygen
N is sodium and O is oxygen
Na is sodium, O2 is oxygen
mcqs.explain: Na represents an atom of sodium and O an atom of oxygen.

mcqs.q: About how many different elements are there, and where are they shown?
options: About 100 elements and compounds, shown in the table
About 20 elements only, all shown in the periodic table
About 100 elements, all shown in the periodic table
Many thousands of elements, most not in the table
mcqs.explain: Matches the specification: about 100 elements, shown in the periodic table.

mcqs.q: Which statement about a compound is correct?
options: Its elements can be mixed together in any proportions at all
Its elements keep all the properties they had before mixing
Its elements can be separated from it by simple filtration
Its elements are chemically combined in fixed proportions
mcqs.explain: Compounds contain two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

mcqs.q: What must happen in every chemical reaction?
options: A detectable energy change must be measured
One or more new substances must always be formed
A gas or a change of colour must be seen
Two elements must join to make a compound
mcqs.explain: Chemical reactions always involve the formation of one or more new substances.

mcqs.q: How can a compound be separated into its elements?
options: Only by using a chemical reaction
By filtering it through filter paper
By evaporating the liquid away from it
By distilling the compound in a flask
mcqs.explain: Compounds can only be separated into elements by chemical reactions.

mcqs.q: Magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid to form magnesium chloride and hydrogen. Which is the correct word equation?
options: magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + water
Mg + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen
magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen
magnesium + acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen
mcqs.explain: Reactant names on the left, product names on the right, all written as words.

mcqs.q: A compound has the formula MgO. What is its name?
options: Magnesium oxygen
Magnesium oxide
Magnesium dioxide
Magnesium peroxide
mcqs.explain: The metal keeps its name and oxygen becomes oxide.

mcqs.q: Magnesium burns in oxygen to form magnesium oxide. Which symbol equation represents this reaction correctly?
options: Mg + O₂ → MgO
Mg + O₂ → MgO₂
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2Mg + 2O₂ → 2MgO
mcqs.explain: Two Mg atoms and two O atoms on each side, with the products on the right.

mcqs.q: (HT only) Molten lead bromide is electrolysed. Which half equation shows what happens at the positive electrode?
options: 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + e⁻
Br⁻ + e⁻ → Br₂
Br⁻ → Br + e⁻
2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻
mcqs.explain: Two bromide ions lose two electrons and form a bromine molecule.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes a mixture?
options: Two or more substances that are chemically combined
Two substances whose properties have both changed
Two or more substances not chemically combined
Two elements joined in fixed proportions by mass
mcqs.explain: A mixture consists of elements or compounds not chemically combined together.

mcqs.q: A mixture of ethanol and water is separated by fractional distillation. Which statement is correct?
options: New substances are made because the mixture has been heated up
The ethanol collected has different properties from before
The two liquids react with each other as they are heated
No new substances are made, as no chemical reaction happens
mcqs.explain: Separation methods are physical processes, so no new substances are made.

mcqs.q: Sand is stirred into salty water and the mixture is filtered. What is left on the filter paper?
options: The sand only, because it does not dissolve
The sand and the salt, which are both solids
The salty water, which stays in the paper
Nothing at all, as sand dissolves in water
mcqs.explain: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid, so the sand is the residue.

mcqs.q: Copper sulfate solution is left in an evaporating basin until crystals form. What has happened?
options: The copper sulfate evaporated, leaving the water behind
The water has evaporated, leaving the copper sulfate
The copper sulfate has reacted to make a blue solid
The water was condensed on a lid and collected
mcqs.explain: In crystallisation the solvent evaporates and the solute is left as crystals.

mcqs.q: Sea water is separated by simple distillation. Which statement is correct?
options: Salt boils off, then condenses and is collected
Both parts boil off at different temperatures
Water evaporates and is lost, leaving the salt
Water boils off, condenses and is collected
mcqs.explain: The solvent evaporates, is condensed and collected, and the salt stays behind.

mcqs.q: A student wants to find out how many coloured dyes are in a sample of ink. Which technique should be used?
options: Filtration using filter paper and a glass funnel
Fractional distillation of the ink sample
Paper chromatography with a suitable solvent
Crystallisation in an evaporating basin
mcqs.explain: Chromatography separates the dyes by how far each one moves with the solvent.

mcqs.q: Which statement about scientific models is correct?
options: New experimental evidence may lead to a model being replaced
Once a model has been accepted it can no longer be changed
A model changes when a scientist prefers a different idea
A model that explains most results is never questioned
mcqs.explain: This is the specification statement about how scientific models change.

mcqs.q: What were atoms thought to be like before the electron was discovered?
options: Tiny spheres with a nucleus in the middle
Balls of negative charge holding protons
Spheres with electrons in set orbits
Tiny spheres that could not be divided
mcqs.explain: Before the discovery of the electron, atoms were thought to be indivisible spheres.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the plum pudding model of the atom?
options: A ball of negative charge with positive particles inside it
A ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it
A small positive nucleus with electrons around the outside
A solid sphere of matter that cannot be divided at all
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's description of the plum pudding model.

mcqs.q: What conclusion came from the results of the alpha particle scattering experiment?
options: The positive charge is spread evenly through the whole atom
The atom is a solid ball of matter with no gaps in it
Electrons in the atom deflect the alpha particles back
The mass of an atom is concentrated at a charged centre
mcqs.explain: The results led to the conclusion that the mass is concentrated at a charged nucleus.

mcqs.q: In the scattering experiment a few alpha particles were deflected straight back. Why did this change the atomic model?
options: It showed that the whole atom is filled with positive charge
It showed that electrons are far heavier than was thought
The plum pudding model could not explain such large deflections
It proved that atoms are tiny spheres that cannot be split
mcqs.explain: A spread-out positive charge could not turn a fast alpha particle around.

mcqs.q: What is the main difference between the plum pudding model and the nuclear model?
options: In the nuclear model the mass and charge are in the nucleus
In the plum pudding model the electrons orbit a small nucleus
In the nuclear model the electrons are embedded in positive charge
In the nuclear model the mass is spread evenly through the atom
mcqs.explain: The nuclear model concentrates the mass and the positive charge at the centre.

mcqs.q: What did Niels Bohr suggest, and how did his idea compare with experiment?
options: Electrons orbit at specific distances, and his calculations agreed with observations
Electrons orbit at specific distances, but no experimental observations supported this
The nucleus exists, and his calculations agreed with the observations
Electrons sit inside the nucleus, and the calculations matched results
mcqs.explain: Bohr adapted the nuclear model, and his theoretical calculations agreed with experimental observations.

mcqs.q: What did later experiments show about the positive charge of a nucleus?
options: It can be divided into whole numbers of identical charges
It is carried by one single particle found by James Chadwick
It comes from the neutrons, which each carry a small charge
It is spread evenly through the atom, not in a nucleus
mcqs.explain: Each of these identical smaller charges was named a proton.

mcqs.q: What did the experimental work of James Chadwick provide evidence for?
options: Protons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after this was accepted
Neutrons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after it was accepted
Electrons, which had been found long before the nuclear model
Electron orbits at set distances from a charged nucleus
mcqs.explain: Chadwick's work showed that neutrons exist within the nucleus.

mcqs.q: What are the relative electrical charges of a proton, a neutron and an electron?
options: Proton and neutron +1, electron −1
Proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1
Proton 0, neutron +1 and electron −1
Every particle has a charge of +1 or −1
mcqs.explain: These are the relative electrical charges given in the specification.

mcqs.q: An atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does it have, and why?
options: 0, because neutrons make the atom neutral overall
22, because protons and electrons are added together
10, because an atom always loses one electron
11, because electrons and protons are equal in number
mcqs.explain: In an atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

mcqs.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
options: The total of the protons and neutrons
The number of protons in each atom
The number of neutrons inside each atom
The number of shells the atom has
mcqs.explain: The number of protons in an atom of an element is its atomic number.

mcqs.q: Two atoms each have 6 protons but different masses. What must be true?
options: They are atoms of different elements
They must have equal numbers of neutrons
They are atoms of the same element
They must have exactly the same mass number
mcqs.explain: All atoms of a particular element have the same number of protons.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
options: 0.1 nm (1 x 10⁻¹⁰ m)
mcqs.explain: This is the value given in the specification.

mcqs.q: How does the radius of a nucleus compare with the radius of the atom?
options: Less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom
About 1/10 of the radius of the whole atom
About the same as the radius of the atom
About half the radius of the whole atom
mcqs.explain: The specification gives less than 1/10 000, about 1 x 10⁻¹⁴ m.

mcqs.q: An atom is imagined to be as wide as a sports stadium. On this scale, about how large is the nucleus?
options: About the size of the whole football pitch
About the size of one of the stands
About the size of a pea in the middle
About the size of half the stadium
mcqs.explain: The nucleus radius is less than 1/10 000 of the atom's, so it is minute on this scale.

mcqs.q: Why is almost all of the mass of an atom in the nucleus?
options: The nucleus takes up nearly all of the atom's volume
Protons and electrons have equal masses but opposite charges
Only neutrons in the nucleus have any mass at all
Protons and neutrons have a relative mass of 1 each
mcqs.explain: The nucleus holds all the protons and neutrons, which carry the mass.

mcqs.q: What are the relative masses of a proton, a neutron and an electron?
options: Proton 1, neutron 1, electron very small
Proton 1, neutron 1, electron also 1
Proton 1, neutron 1 and electron 0 exactly
Proton 1, neutron very small and electron 1
mcqs.explain: These are the relative masses given in the specification.

mcqs.q: What is the mass number of an atom?
options: The sum of its protons and electrons
The sum of its protons and neutrons
The number of protons that it contains
The number of neutrons it contains
mcqs.explain: The specification defines the mass number as the sum of the protons and neutrons.

mcqs.q: What are isotopes?
options: Atoms of the same element but with different numbers of protons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of electrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of different elements with the same mass number
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition of isotopes.

mcqs.q: A chlorine atom is written with mass number 35 and atomic number 17. What does it contain?
options: 17 protons, 35 neutrons, plus 17 electrons
35 protons, with 17 neutrons and 35 electrons
18 protons, 17 neutrons, 17 electrons
17 protons, 18 neutrons and 17 electrons
mcqs.explain: Protons = 17, neutrons = 35 − 17 = 18, and electrons equal protons.

mcqs.q: A chloride ion is written Cl⁻. A chlorine atom has atomic number 17. Which is correct for the ion?
options: 17 protons and 16 electrons, since one is lost
18 protons and 18 electrons, since it is neutral
17 protons and 17 electrons, as they stay equal
17 protons and 18 electrons, as one is gained
mcqs.explain: The 1− charge shows one extra electron; the number of protons is unchanged.

mcqs.q: What does the relative atomic mass of an element take account of?
options: The abundance of each of its isotopes
The mass number of its commonest isotope
The average of its isotope mass numbers
The number of protons in each of its atoms
mcqs.explain: Relative atomic mass is an average that takes account of isotope abundance.

mcqs.q: Lithium has two isotopes: 7.5% is ⁶Li and 92.5% is ⁷Li. What is the relative atomic mass of lithium?
In which order do electrons occupy the energy levels (shells) of an atom?
options: The outer shell is filled before the inner ones
They spread out evenly between the shells
The lowest available energy level is filled first
The first shell takes eight electrons first
mcqs.explain: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels, the innermost available shells.

mcqs.q: A magnesium atom has 12 electrons. Which electronic structure is correct?
mcqs.explain: Two electrons fill the first level and eight the second, leaving two in the third.

mcqs.q: The electronic structure of sodium is 2,8,1. What does the final 1 tell you?
options: There is one electron in the third energy level
There is one electron in the innermost shell only
One of the shells in the atom is completely full
One electron is left over without a shell
mcqs.explain: The numbers are read outwards, so the last one is the outermost level.

mcqs.q: Why is the electronic structure of sodium 2,8,1 rather than 2,9?
options: The second energy level always holds nine electrons
The second energy level holds only eight electrons
The outer energy level is always filled up first of all
The numbers are read from the outside of the atom inwards
mcqs.explain: Once the second level holds eight, the next electron starts the third level.

mcqs.q: A fluorine atom has 9 electrons. Which shell diagram is correct?
options: 2 on the first ring and 7 on the second
8 on the first ring and 1 on the second
7 on the first ring and 2 on the second
5 on the first ring and 4 on the second
mcqs.explain: The first energy level is full with two electrons, so the other seven go in the second.

mcqs.q: A shell diagram is drawn with 4 electrons on the outer ring, 8 on the middle ring and 2 on the inner ring. Which electronic structure does it show?
mcqs.explain: The structure starts at the innermost ring: 2, then 8, then 4.

mcqs.q: (HT only) Silver nitrate solution reacts with sodium chloride solution: AgNO₃(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃(aq). Which is the correct ionic equation?
options: Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s)
Ag⁺(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s)
AgNO₃(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s)
Na⁺(aq) + NO₃⁻(aq) → NaNO₃(aq)
mcqs.explain: Only these ions change; Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ are spectator ions and are left out.

mcqs.q: Ink is spotted on chromatography paper and a solvent runs up it. Why do the dyes separate?
options: They move different distances with the solvent
The darkest dye always travels the furthest
The paper traps each dye as a filter would
The paper reacts with the dyes to make new ones
mcqs.explain: Each dye is held by the paper and carried by the solvent to a different extent.

mcqs.q: A mixture of ethanol and water is separated by fractional distillation. Why does this method work?
options: The two liquids boil at different temperatures
One is a solid dissolved in the other liquid
Heating the mixture makes new substances form
Water evaporates away, leaving the ethanol
mcqs.explain: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids using their different boiling points.
